stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: The State High-Level Clearance Committee (SHLCC), chaired by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, on Wednesday approved nine new projects and eight proposals for additional investments, involving a total investment of Rs 29,679 crore in Karnataka’s industrial sector. The projects are expected to create 66,360 jobs..Under the new investment projects, Vibrancy Renewable Energies will invest Rs 2,194.94 crore and provide employment to 30,000 people. Mahindra Aerostructures will invest Rs 2,300 crore, creating 3,000 jobs; Aequs Consumer Products will invest Rs 1,104 crore, creating 4,813 jobs; Hero Future Energies will invest Rs 9,760 crore and create 3,200 jobs..Epsilon will invest Rs 1,500 crore, Toyota Kirloskar Rs 1,200 crore, Nirani Sugars Rs 4,062 crore, TruAlt Bioenergy Rs 2,988 crore and Lighthouse Alternative Assets Rs 600 crore..Karnataka: BJP's BY Vijayendra seeks white paper on sources of funds for guarantees.MSPL will make an additional investment of Rs 884.25 crore; Reliance Power Solutions Rs 250 crore, Honda Cars Rs 437 crore, Bhima Fine Chemicals Rs 605 crore, Sansera Rs 492.24 crore;, TVS Motors Rs 1,050 crore and Havells India Rs 250 crore..The Chief Minister directed officials of the Finance Department to thoroughly scrutinise project reports submitted for granting industrial licences. He said a pre-clearance audit should be made mandatory for projects and instructed officials to constitute a new audit team for this purpose..He also directed officials to ensure strict compliance with all provisions of the industrial policy and take all necessary measures to encourage the establishment and expansion of industries in the state..Ministers M B Patil, K J George, Priyank Kharge, Ajay Singh and P M Narendra Swamy; Chief Secretary Shalini Rajneesh; Chief Minister’s Economic Adviser L K Atheeq; Additional Chief Secretary Tushar Girinath; Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, Selvakumar; and other senior officials were present at the meeting.

stories.headline: How valuable are mangroves? Study on Pichavaram ecosystem pegs it at ₹2,485.38 crore
stories.deck: Mangrove ecosystems provide a wide range of provisioning, regulating, supporting, and cultural ecosystem services that contribute significantly to ecological sustainability and human well-being
stories.bodyText:
Ecosystem service-wise economic value (in ₹ crore)
How valuable are mangroves? A recent study of the Pichavaram mangrove ecosystem estimated its Total Economic Value (TEV) at ₹2,485.38 crore ($289 million), with a per-hectare value of ₹1.83 crore, reflecting the ecological, economic and social benefits it provides.
The Pichavaram Mangrove Forest is deemed one of the most ecologically significant coastal wetland ecosystems in India and plays a vital role in supporting biodiversity conservation, fisheries productivity, coastal protection, climate regulation, blue carbon sequestration, and livelihood security for coastal communities.
“Mangrove ecosystems provide a wide range of provisioning, regulating, supporting, and cultural ecosystem services that contribute significantly to ecological sustainability and human well-being. Despite their importance, many ecosystem services remain undervalued in conventional development planning because several ecological benefits are non-market in nature and are not reflected in market transactions,” says the study, ’Economic Valuation and Blue Carbon Assessment of Ecosystem Services (ESV) in the Pichavaram Mangrove Forest’.
Increasing climate change impacts, biodiversity loss, and coastal vulnerability have further emphasised the need for comprehensive assessment of the ecological and economic contributions of mangrove ecosystems, it added.
In 2024, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), in what it termed the
The study, by M. Balasubramanian, associate professor, Centre for Ecological Economics and Natural Resources, Institute for Social and Economic Change, Bengaluru, was funded by the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Forest Genetics Division, Coimbatore. It was based on primary and secondary data; primary information was collected from 302 households across five mangrove-dependent villages: MGR Thittu, Kalaignar Nagar, Chinnavaikal, Patriadi, and Mudasalodai.
Carbon reservoir
“The blue carbon assessment highlights the critical role of the Pichavaram Mangrove Ecosystem as a significant natural carbon sink and a valuable climate regulation asset. Field measurements and carbon stock analysis indicated that the mangrove vegetation stores an average of 79.449 tonnes of carbon per hectare, equivalent to approximately 291.33 tonnes of CO2 per hectare,” says the study.
The analysis further revealed that mangrove sediments constitute an even more substantial carbon reservoir. The average soil organic carbon stock of 251.14 tonnes of carbon per hectare was estimated to generate an economic value of ₹90.24 lakh per hectare, resulting in a total soil organic carbon value of ₹1,224.63 crore. When vegetation and soil carbon pools are combined, the total blue carbon asset value of the Pichavaram Mangrove Ecosystem is estimated at ₹1,612.40 crore
“These findings clearly demonstrate that the majority of blue carbon is stored below ground in mangrove sediments, emphasising the importance of conserving both mangrove vegetation and soil systems. The substantial blue carbon value underscores the ecosystem’s contribution to climate regulation, carbon sequestration, and long-term ecological sustainability, while also providing strong justification for integrating mangroves into climate finance mechanisms, blue carbon initiatives, and natural capital accounting frameworks,” the study added.
Integration
The study recommends the integration of ecosystem service valuation into coastal development planning and environmental decision-making, recognition of mangroves as critical nature-based solutions for climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction, and the development of blue carbon financing mechanisms, carbon credit programmes, and Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) schemes.
It also advocates the incorporation of mangrove values into the Natural Capital Accounting and Green GDP frameworks, the promotion of sustainable livelihood opportunities through fisheries, eco-tourism, community-based conservation, and mangrove restoration, and strengthening climate resilience and biodiversity conservation through long-term ecosystem-based management strategies.

stories.headline: 'Look at what the rankings were before': PCB chief Naqvi hits back at critics
stories.deck: Pakistan Cricket Board Chairman Mohsin Naqvi defended sweeping Test squad and coaching changes after Pakistan’s heavy 2-0 series loss to England. Seven players were dropped and five uncapped players added, while Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke took coaching roles. Despite criticism from former cricketers and fans, Naqvi called the decisions "essential" and defended his record, highlighting progress…
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) Chairman Mohsin Naqvi has defended the major changes made to 
Pakistan
’s Test squad during the ongoing England series, saying the decisions were "essential".
Pakistan made sweeping changes before the third and final Test against England, scheduled to begin on September 9.
The move came after Pakistan lost the first two Tests heavily, with England taking an unassailable 2-0 lead. Pakistan lost the first Test by an innings, while the second ended in a 194-run defeat.
Naqvi responds to criticism
The changes have drawn strong criticism from former Pakistan cricketers, fans and analysts. However, Naqvi said he was not concerned by the backlash and maintained that the decisions during the England tour were necessary.
He said he was also examining issues beyond the team's poor performances but believed it was not the right time to discuss matters unrelated to cricket. While acknowledging Pakistan’s disappointing Test results, Naqvi pointed to improvements in the team’s white-ball cricket during his tenure.
"I have never been afraid of criticism, and I never will be. Those who say cricket has been destroyed since I came - look at what the rankings were before," he said as quoted by Geo News.
Major changes to Test squad
Following the second loss, the PCB released seven players from the squad: Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Agha, Ali Usman, Aamer Jamal, Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad.
The board replaced them with five uncapped players, along with Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, who together have only 10 matches of experience. The new players include Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran Randhawa and Razaullah.
The PCB also made changes to the coaching staff, bringing in Mike Hesson as head coach and Ashley Noffke as bowling coach. Both are already part of Pakistan’s white-ball coaching set-up. Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were released from their respective coaching roles.

briefs.headline: Five dead, 30 injured in bus-truck collision in M.P.’s Rewa
briefs.deck: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav expressed grief over the accident and announced ₹2 lakh assistance for the families of the deceased and ₹1 lakh for the seriously injured
briefs.bodyText:
Five persons were killed and 30 others injured after a bus collided with a truck on a national highway in the Rewa district of Madhya Pradesh on Wednesday (September 2, 2026), police said.
The accident took place around 4:30 p.m. on National Highway 39 near Badwar, located under the Gudh police station area, about 30 kilometres from the district headquarters, a senior official said.
The accident scene dissolved into chaos as the victims’ screams filled the air. Locals immediately began relief work and informed the police.
Soon after being informed, police and administration teams arrived at the scene and launched relief and rescue operations. Several ambulances were dispatched to transport the injured to the hospital.
Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Bhavana Maravi told PTI Videos, “Five people died in the accident, while 30 others were injured.” She said all the injured were shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital in Rewa, where they are undergoing treatment.
Rescue operations are still underway at the scene, and efforts are on to ensure that nobody is trapped in the bus, she said.
Maravi said the impact was so severe that the truck overturned and the bus fell into a water-filled drain.
Chief Minister Mohan Yadav expressed grief over the accident and said the state government has issued instructions to provide financial assistance of ₹2 lakh each to the families of the deceased and ₹1 lakh each to the seriously injured.
In a post on X, he said, “The news of the deaths of passengers in the collision between a bus and a dumper on the Rewa-Sidhi highway today is extremely heartbreaking. I pray for the peace of the departed souls and a speedy recovery for the injured.” Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Anurag Tiwari said additional beds have been reserved in the hospital so that other injured people can also be treated immediately if required.
The police are investigating the cause of the accident, he said.
National Highway 39 connects Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh to Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, and passes through Madhya Pradesh.

briefs.headline: West Asia conflict updates: Iran blacklists more ships trying to sail through Hormuz, govt. website shows
briefs.deck: Iran security chief says U.S. to face new war strategy; Bessent warns 'everyone' against backing Tehran
briefs.bodyText:
Iran threatened to take a tougher line in its war with the United States on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) after the heaviest exchanges in weeks left at least 19 Iranians dead, including four at a wedding -- an incident slammed as a “war crime” by Tehran. A wave of Iranian attacks earlier targeted US bases in Jordan, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, after extensive U.S. bombardment hit sites across Iran.
Watch | U.S., Iran exchange fresh strikes near Strait of Hormuz
U.S. President Donald Trump had warned earlier of “much harder and higher” attacks if Iran retaliated to the U.S. strikes, which Iran’s military and state media said killed 18 people. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesperson Tim Hawkins said “the U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC”, referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.
The latest flare-up is part of a cycle of retaliation that followed U.S. strikes on Iran, with fighting over the Hormuz strait expanding to Washington’s Gulf allies, military bases and commercial shipping. It began when Washington hit Iranian targets on Sunday (August 30, 2026), the first known strikes in several weeks, after which Tehran’s forces targeted US troops in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, and projectiles struck two oil tankers in unclaimed attacks.

briefs.headline: Two dead, multiple injured in Minneapolis shooting
briefs.deck: The suspect was also dead, Spokesperson for the police Garrett Parten said at a press conference, adding that it wasn’t clear how he had died
briefs.bodyText:
Two people have died and several more were injured, including three police officers, when a gunman opened fire in the U.S. city of Minneapolis on Wednesday (September 2, 2027), police said.
The suspect was also dead, Garrett Parten, a spokesperson for the police, said at a press conference, adding that it wasn’t clear how he had died.
One person died at the scene, Parten added. Four people were taken to hospital, where one later died.
Also taken to the hospital were three police officers, including two who were shot. Both were expected to survive, with a hospital spokesperson telling AFP that they were in “stable condition”.
One was shot in the leg, while another was in surgery. It was not clear what injury the third officer sustained.
There was no mention of motive during the press conference.
Governor Tim Walz asked the public to “pray for Minnesota”, while FBI Director Kash Patel said his agents were responding.
City officials are expected to hold a press conference later on Wednesday (September 2, 2027).

Pawan Kalyan aide, Tollywood's popular art director Anand Sai's son held in hit & run case, out on bail
briefs.bodyText: Hyderabad: Hyderabad police have arrested Sandeep Anand, the 23-year-old son of popular Tollywood art director Anand Sai, in connection with a fatal accident on August 31 that allegedly killed one person. Sandeep was arrested on Tuesday evening and released on bail from a local court on Wednesday. According to Raidurgam police, the accident occurred around 4:15 am on August 31, when 31-year-old Nanda Kishor Kumar Ray was crossing the road opposite Ankura Hospital in Khajaguda. He was initially hit by an Innova Crysta approaching from the Nanakramguda ORR Rotary. Ray, a native of Bihar, had been working as a chef at a nearby restaurant for a few months. .Pawan Kalyan says he wanted to join the Naxalites at 17, but Chiranjeevi stopped him.The Innova's driver, 21-year-old Zaid Shah Qadri, stopped at the scene and, along with a passer-by, attempted to carry the injured man to a hospital. As the three were crossing the road, two vehicles speeding from Khajaguda toward the Nanakramguda ORR Rotary allegedly ran into them before fleeing the scene. Ray died on the spot, while Qadri suffered a leg fracture and other injuries and was admitted to a hospital in Gachibowli. Acting on information from locals, police reached the scene, registered a case and launched an investigation, scanning CCTV footage along the stretch between Khajaguda and the Nanakramguda Financial District. This led them to one of the two vehicles a Mahindra XUV electric car traced to Sandeep, who was arrested on Tuesday and had his vehicle seized. A young man named Sourya, who was driving the second car, was also taken into custody. The two are reportedly friends. . Sandeep has been booked under Section 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) a bailable provision covering death caused by negligence along with Sections 125(a) and 281 of the BNS, and Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Anand Sai, a close aide of Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, also serves on the TTD Board as member and is known for his architectural work on the redevelopment of Telangana's popular hill shrine, Yadagirigutta.

stories.headline: Rajasthan teenager caught in Bengaluru for creating fake Facebook account in IPS officer’s name
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A 17-year-old from 
Rajasthan
 was caught for allegedly creating a fake Facebook account in the name of an IPS officer here and collecting money from people.
The fake account was in the name of IPS officer Narayana M, deputy commissioner of police, Electronics City division.
The fraud was exposed in July when a victim filed a police complaint stating miscreants had opened a Facebook account in Narayan’s name and a friend request was sent to him. “Using my mobile number, the miscreant said a CRPF constable was selling household articles for a low price and I should buy them. I was asked to pay Rs 40,000 as advance. Later I realised it was a con game,” the victim told police.
Police recovered Rs 2 lakh in cash from the juvenile, which was allegedly part of the money fraudulently obtained through fake bank accounts. “During interrogation, the teenager confessed to have committed the offence along with a few associates. He said he created fake Facebook accounts in the names of several IAS and IPS officers across the country and were collecting money by impersonating them,” a police officer said.

stories.headline: Pink Line elevated stretch in Bengaluru nears launch; Two clearances remain
stories.bodyText:
BMRCL Plans To Run Train Services With A Frequency Of 6 Minutes
Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development inspecting BMRCL Pink lane in Bengaluru on Wednesday, with Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya and other officials
Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development inspecting BMRCL Pink lane in Bengaluru on Wednesday, with Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya and other officials
The 7.5-km elevated stretch of Namma Metro’s Pink Line, from Tavarekere to Kalena Agrahara, is ready for opening, with the launch awaiting two key statutory approvals, according to Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL).
The metro operator expects the Railway Board’s approval for the new rolling stock shortly. Once secured, the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (CMRS) will inspect the stretch and grant the mandatory safety clearance for commercial operations. BMRCL is targeting Sept for the opening.
Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda inspected the line Wednesday, travelling from Jayadeva interchange station, serving Yellow and Pink Lines, to Kalena Agrahara. Bengaluru South MP 
Tejasvi Surya
, Bangalore South MLA A Krishnappa and BMRCL managing director PC Jaffer accompanied him.
Byre Gowda said the 7.5-km elevated section of Pink Line is ready for commercial operations. “As soon as the date is given by the Union govt, this stretch will be inaugurated and opened for public use. We are hopeful that we will get a date for the inauguration within Sept,” he said.
Surya said: “I spoke to CMRS officials regarding the safety clearances and timelines. Rolling stock approval is expected within 15 days, followed by clearance for the entire line. 
I will work with officials and the central govt to ensure these approvals are secured at the earliest.”
BMRCL officials said sufficient trains were available for the six-station section, with services planned every six minutes. The trains are undergoing prescribed trials and must complete mandatory 750-km travel before passenger deployment. Train operators have been identified, with mandatory training expected to conclude this week.
During the inspection, officials briefed the minister about the new train sets manufactured by BEML, which have around 70% local components. The trains are equipped to support Automatic Train Operation (ATO) and advanced Unattended Train Operation (UTO), enabling them to operate without a driver.
At Kalena Agrahara Metro station, officials briefed the minister on the advanced Communication-Based Train Control (CBTC) signalling system, the Station Control Room, and the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system integrated with National Common Mobility Card (NCMC).

stories.headline: Proposed economic masterplan for Bengaluru Metropolitan Region targets 75% public transport
stories.deck: The plan, a draft of which was presented to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, proposes expanding metro, suburban rail, and regional rapid transit system corridors
stories.bodyText:
While the Karnataka government is moving ahead with big-ticket infrastructure projects for private transport for Bengaluru, a proposed economic master plan for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region (BMR) has set an ambitious target of increasing the share of public transport from 35% to 75%.
The plan, a draft of which was presented to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Wednesday, proposes expanding metro, suburban rail, and regional rapid transit system (RRTS) corridors, besides building a second airport, strengthening ring, radial and chord roads, and developing multi-modal hubs.
The transport proposal is part of a larger plan to take the BMR’s economy from the current $149 billion to $400 billion by 2037, while creating up to 2.5 million jobs.
Prepared by the Karnataka government with the ISEG Foundation, the plan identifies five areas that it expects to drive the region’s growth — technology, high-tech manufacturing, healthcare and education, infrastructure and sustainability, and planned urbanisation and housing.
The BMR covers three districts and has around 16 million people. It accounts for about 40% of Karnataka’s Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) despite having around a quarter of the State’s population, while its per capita income is nearly twice the State average.
The plan proposes making BMR a major technology hub by developing dedicated IT and global capability centre (GCC) hubs, deep-tech sandboxes, and a dedicated AI mission. It also proposes a high-tech manufacturing hub, with aerospace and Defence, among the priority sectors for the region. Healthcare, higher education, and high-end tourism have also been identified as areas for growth.
For urban development, it proposes planned cities, services-led business districts, integrated private townships, and transit-oriented development. It also calls for affordable and shared rental housing for industrial, gig and service workers, besides a slum rehabilitation programme aimed at making the BMR slum-free.
The plan also proposes attracting private investment at scale and using increases in land value to help fund the region’s development. The recommendations will be discussed with the relevant departments before the plan is finalised.

stories.headline: Chicken shops in Bengaluru to shut over waste disposal fee
stories.bodyText:
Chicken shops across Bengaluru, associated with the Karnataka Poultry Traders Association (KPTA), will shut down for two days starting September 3, to protest against the ₹5-per-kg service fee that Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd. (BSWML) is set to charge for collecting poultry waste generated by meat shops.
The association has demanded that a minimum support price be fixed for poultry waste, arguing that the waste has ‘commercial value’ and is used by private companies to manufacture by-products and animal feed, which are then sold for profit.
“Waste such as intestines, feathers, skin, and bones is taken by private companies, which process it into powder and use it to make products such as dog and cat food. They earn from these products. At present, middlemen collect the waste from us and earn from it, while the companies also make a profit from the final product using our raw material,” the association said.
The association argued that instead of charging shops ₹5 per kg for the waste, private companies should purchase it from them at a minimum support price. On an average, each chicken shop generates around 32 kg to 35 kg of such waste, the association said.
It also pointed to a tender notification issued by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), which states that an authorised service provider has been appointed by BSWML for the scientific collection, transportation and processing of poultry, fish, pig, and other animal waste, including animal bones, generated within the GBA limits.
The notification states that all meat, poultry, fish, pork shops, and other establishments generating animal waste will have to mandatorily pay a service fee of ₹5 per kg for animal waste and ₹3 per kg for animal bone waste to the authorised service providers. It also requires establishments to hand over the waste only to service providers officially appointed by BSWML.
The association, however, said the fee would add to the costs of chicken shops. It said that if the government does not consider its demand for a minimum support price, shopkeepers would be forced to increase the price of chicken to recover the additional cost.

briefs.headline: Four lakh students to become Karnataka’s potential blood donor pool
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Four lakh students could soon form one of Karnataka’s largest organised pools of blood donors, with Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) planning to create a digital repository that can connect those willing to donate for patients in need.
Called ‘Raktha Kosh’, the proposed platform will tap into RGUHS’s vast student network spread across the state. The idea is simple: when a student enrols in a college, if they are eligible and willing to donate, can register themselves as donors on the platform. When a particular blood group is urgently required or there is a shortage in a locality, registered donors will receive a notification and they can proceed to the nearest blood bank or hospital. The platform will also connect them with district officials, local ambulance and emergency services so that they can deliver it to the needy immediately.
Additionally, it will also look at bringing all the registries under one roof. “Blood donors registries are being maintained by various NGO, health science institutions and voluntary donors’ organisations. However, they are spread unevenly across the state. 
In addition, it is also observed that availability of rare blood group donors is also not maintained in all the blood donors’ registries. Keeping these things in view, it is proposed not only to establish blood donor’s registry at RGUHS, but also integrate all the blood banks, registries as one integrated registry so that the availability of blood at emergency situation, particularly rare blood groups is ensured,” said vice chancellor Bhagvan BC.
“With the increase in the incidence of thalassemia, road accidents, and the enhanced need for blood donations during emergencies, it is difficult to find out the blood donors during such situations. At the same time, there is also an issue of wastage of blood, with it crossing the expiry. This repository will help in that cause too,” he added.
The recent syndicate meeting also unanimously approved the idea. Approval from competent authorities will be taken prior to the establishment of the registry. “Our idea is to build a software to manage the repository. Our biggest strength is our human resource. Our presence is there in every district. We will leverage that,” the VC said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka CM tells womenpreneurs: Speak up for tunnel road, traffic solutions
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: “Shout at me if I’m doing wrong,” Karnataka chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 declared at a business summit here Wednesday, placing 
women entrepreneurs
 front and centre of urban traffic and civic infrastructure projects and urging them to become partners in Karnataka’s growth story.
Asking them to publicly support his government’s controversial tunnel-road project from Hebbal to Silk Board, the CM said some leaders were opposing it for political reasons. He maintained that the tunnel would pass beneath Lalbagh without damaging its green asset, a contrasting stand 24 hours after agreeing to revisit a now-passed bill to set aside 5% of park land for infrastructure projects.
Addressing the fifth edition of ‘Together We Grow’, organised by Ubuntu Consortium at FKCCI, Shivakumar said Bengaluru’s mobility problems were impacting business and workers in terms of time and money. He asked the gathering to speak up on the issue and hold political leaders accountable.
In a strong defence of tunnel projects, Shivakumar explained the rationale behind such proposals: Widening existing roads is difficult because much of Bengaluru has not been planned for its present scale. Travelling from Mysuru to Bengaluru takes 90 minutes, but entering the city and reaching the final destination could take longer, he said.
He said the government was investing more than Rs 1.5 lakh crore in Bengaluru’s development and mobility infrastructure. The city’s rapid growth and rising number of vehicles had made travel increasingly difficult, he admitted.
The remarks come amid opposition to the proposed north-south tunnel corridor project, which is facing criticism from BJP, civic groups and urban-mobility experts. Critics have questioned its cost and argued that car-focused infrastructure could undermine Bengaluru’s public-transport goals.
At the event, the chief minister also assured women entrepreneurs of all govt support. “You are not employees, you are employers,” he said, praising them for creating jobs and assuming a wider responsibility towards society.
Shivakumar pointed to the state’s subsidised financing facility under which eligible women entrepreneurs can access Karnataka State Financial Corporation loans at an effective interest rate of 4%. He called for more educated women to enter politics and assume leadership roles from gram panchayats to Parliament.

briefs.headline: Give suggestions on parking rules for Greater Bengaluru Authority till Sept 10
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka govt has invited public suggestions on its draft comprehensive parking rules for Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), with stakeholders and citizens given time till Sept 10 to submit their feedback.
The rules propose annual parking permit fee, ranging from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 depending on the type of car, for parking vehicles in front of their houses.
The draft includes incentives to encourage vacant sites to be converted into organised parking facilities, including 100% property tax exemption for sites used for multi-level or mechanised parking and 50% exemption for those used for surface parking.
The rules also propose a fee-based parking system, with tariffs based on factors such as road classification and location of parking facilities. Monthly passes will be available for regular off-street parking users.
On-street parking will be prohibited on highly congested arterial roads and could be restricted during peak hours on major stretches. Parking will be prohibited around designated multi-level car parking facilities, while longer parking durations will attract higher charges.
The draft proposes stronger enforcement against building owners who fail to provide parking mandated under building regulations or misuse designated parking spaces for other purposes.
Suggestions can be emailed to acsuddoffice@gmail.com or submitted to additional chief secretary, urban development department, Vikasa Soudha, by Sept 10.

briefs.headline: Karnataka clears Rs 30,000-crore projects to create 66,000 jobs
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The state high-level clearance committee headed by chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 Wednesday evening cleared 17 multi-sector projects worth Rs 29,679 crore.
From aerospace to renewable energy and from cars to toys, nine projects are expected to generate 66,360 jobs.
The highest investment comes from Hero Future Energies in renewable energy with Rs 9,760 crore seeking to create 3,200 jobs. Other notable investments are Vibrancy Real Estates, which is investing Rs 2,196 crore, and Mahindra Aerostructures that’s setting up a unit worth Rs 2,300 crore.
Vibrancy Real Estates is said to be a joint venture between real estate giants Brigade Enterprises and alternative investment fund company called GSS India Opportunities managed by Bain Capital Advisors. While this venture is expected to generate 30,000 jobs in the state, Mahindra subsidiary will create 3,000 jobs.
Aequs Consumer Products (Rs 1,104 crore), known for toys, Epsilon Cam (Rs 1,500 crore), Toyota Kirloskar Motor (Rs 1,200 crore), Nirani Sugars (Rs 4,063 crore), TruAlt Bioenergy (Rs 2,988 crore) and Lighthouse Canton Alternative Asset (Rs 600 crore) will be making fresh investments.
The CM-led committee cleared additional projects worth Rs 3,969 crore by eight companies.
Shivakumar instructed officials to ensure proper project checks and pre-audits for granting licences. He is said to have directed the finance department to form a new audit team for the purpose.

briefs.headline: To SIR with anxiety: Karnataka PU students bear the brunt
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: With 50% of lecturers drafted for the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) exercise, nearly 8,000 students of 20 govt PU colleges in Bengaluru are a worried lot over both gaps in academics and incomplete assessments.
Exams are set to begin on Sept 25, but portions are incomplete. Some lecturers who have been relieved of SIR duty have started taking classes again, but others are still stuck with the poll duty.
Some 142 of the 288 lecturers in Bangalore Central educational district have been assigned SIR duty. Some 4,930 in first PU and 2,928 in second PU are studying Arts, Science and Commerce streams in these institutions.
While college principals have flagged concerns, the deputy director of the dept of school education, Bangalore Central educational district, has, in a letter, sought the release of at least half of the lecturers from SIR duty so that the daily activities of the college are not disrupted and classes can be conducted.
“It is unfortunate that the department of school education has not thought about the consequences of this absence of teachers on campuses. They could have recruited additional guest lecturers but no alternative arrangements were made. But at commencement of the admission, they pressured us to increase enrolment. Now parents and students are asking us where the lecturers are,” said AH Ningegowda, president, 
Karnataka
 State Pre-University College Lecturers’ Association.
TOI had reported earlier that experts have warned of learning loss due to long absence of teachers.
Some schools said they have conducted formative assessments (FA), while others haven’t. “We are a nodal centre for SIR duties. All the three teachers are on SIR duty. We have not conducted FAs. How can we conduct assessments? We are unsure of summative assessment since nothing has been taught in classrooms,” said a primary school teacher.
Vikas Kishor Suralkar, commissioner, school education department, said: “As per our data, 10-15% of teachers in Karnataka are on SIR duty. The impact on schools is not unmanageable, but (impact on) Bengaluru could be more. When teachers are back, we’ll hold extra classes. Summative assessment will be held as per schedule.”
“We have been raising the issue of absence of teachers on campuses. Since sports is happening, some schools without PE teachers have regular teachers attending to it. When will they finally find time to teach?” asked Moidin Kutti, president, Karnataka State SDMC Co-ordination Central Forum.

briefs.headline: Why building Bengaluru’s infrastructure is my top priority
briefs.bodyText:
By 
DK Shivakumar
DK Shivakumar, chief minister of Karnataka
Bengaluru’s growth has been one of 
Karnataka
’s greatest economic strengths. Its global reputation in IT, startups, global capability centres, aerospace, biotechnology and emerging technologies draws investment, employment and innovation to the state. As competition for investment grows sharper, Bengaluru must have infrastructure and urban systems to match the scale of activity it can generate. Strengthening the city is not a priority for Bengaluru alone, but an investment in Karnataka’s economic future.
The nature of this competition is quickly changing. Hyderabad is preparing for the next generation of technology and urban infrastructure. Andhra is developing Amaravati while wooing industry, education and healthcare investment. Visakhapatnam is emerging as a hub for advanced technology, with Google announcing a major AI hub there. Tamil Nadu too is attracting investment across electronics, EVs, space tech, quantum computing and life sciences. Competition is no longer confined to IT offices or factories — it now spans AI, cloud infrastructure, data centres, renewable energy and digital infrastructure.
Bengaluru already has what investors seek: A deep talent pool, a mature tech ecosystem, a strong research base and global presence. 
The priority is to ensure its physical and digital infrastructure keeps pace. For a global company evaluating investment, airport connectivity, public transport, reliable power and water, and room for future growth are all part of the decision. Urban infrastructure has become economic infrastructure.
Bengaluru Metro Phase 3 is a key step. The Union cabinet approved the project at Rs 15,611 crore, covering 44.6km across two corridors and 31 stations, taking the network to 220km. This will strengthen links between employment centres, homes, educational institutions and business districts. Road networks too must evolve — tunnel roads on critical corridors, along with the Bengaluru Business Corridor and ring roads, can ease movement and support growth where conventional widening isn’t feasible.
Future growth must be supported by new, well-planned urban centres. The proposed Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township at Bidadi, spread over 7,481 acres in nine villages at an estimated cost of Rs 18,133 crore, is envisaged as a work-live-play hub with housing, offices, industries, schools, hospitals and parks. About 2,000 acres are earmarked for AI and allied industries, aimed at an ecosystem for AI, data infrastructure, R&D and GCCs.
Such development must move forward with public trust at its centre. Concerns of farmers and affected communities over land, compensation and livelihoods must be addressed through a fair, transparent process. Growth and people’s interests are not competing objectives — sustainable development needs both. Every avenue of public funding — central and state — must be leveraged so every rupee converts into infrastructure and opportunity.
Bengaluru’s and Karnataka’s development are not competing priorities but closely linked — a stronger Bengaluru generates momentum, investment and jobs that strengthen the state’s capacity to develop every region.
Bengaluru’s past success cannot be taken for granted; as cities across south India prepare for the next wave of investment, Karnataka must build infrastructure to ensure it continues to lead. A stronger Bengaluru means a stronger Karnataka.
(The writer is chief minister of Karnataka)

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Six past amendments allowed specific park land diversions; new Bill proposes 5% blanket provision
briefs.deck: The new draft Bill introduced during the recently concluded Monsoon Session seeks to allow a general diversion of park land
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, has previously been amended six times to permit the use or alienation of specific portions of government parks for identified public projects. All six alienations have been incorporated as amendments under Section 5 of the Act. However, the new draft Bill introduced during the recently concluded Monsoon Session seeks to allow a general diversion of park land.
The 1975 Act was originally enacted to protect government parks and gardens from being diverted for other uses, but Section 5 was included to provide for specific exemptions. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday said he would examine and discuss why the proposal to allow diversion of 5% of park land was introduced, and also review what the BJP and previous governments had done, and which lands had been allotted to whom in the past.
As per the documents, the earlier approach under Section 5 of the Parks Act was essentially exception-based: a specific parcel was identified, the extent was specified, and the purpose for which it could be used was mentioned in the law. The 2026 amendment adopts a different approach. It retains the existing Section 5 as sub-section (1), but proposes to insert a new sub-section allowing the State government, on the recommendation of a High-Level Committee, to alienate or permit the use of land or buildings in a park for specified public purposes up to 5% of the park’s total area.
Previous permissions
Among the earlier permissions was the alienation of 1,223 sq. metres (0.30 acres) of the Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park near Raj Bhavan Road. The alienation was meant to facilitate road widening by the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike. Another provision allowed 1,135.18 sq. metres (0.280 acres) of Lalbagh along its western boundary to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. for the construction of an elevated metro station. Both amendments were enacted in 2008.
Section 5 also provided for the use of two specified portions of Cubbon Park, measuring 2,126.71 sq. metres (0.52 acres) and 11,160 sq. metres (2.75 acres), with their boundaries specifically identified in the legislation.
Another provision permitted 18,028.35 sq. meters (4.45 acres) between the High Court building and the old KGID building to be used for parking vehicles of High Court advocates and visitors.
The provision further covered 49 acres and 34 guntas, approximately, comprising Vidhana Soudha, Vikasa Soudha, and other structures, allowing the land to be used for repairs and other developmental works.

briefs.headline: SIR: Notices cite errors despite correct details in forms; hearing to begin from Sept. 5 in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Once the process of generating a notice is initiated, it takes a week before a hearing can be held, with the first hearing possible only on the seventh day
briefs.bodyText:
While the disposal of notices in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was supposed to begin on August 24 across Karnataka as per the ECI’s guidelines, Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) in Bengaluru said they generated the notices only on August 28.
Once the process of generating a notice is initiated, it takes a week before a hearing can be held, with the first hearing possible only on the seventh day. In Bengaluru, therefore, hearings can begin only on September 5 — meaning 10 days have already been lost in a process that is already working against a tight deadline.
Huge workload
The hearings will continue until October 22, leaving EROs less than 60 days to conclude cases involving 43.81 lakh voters across Karnataka. Over 24 lakh of these cases are concentrated in Bengaluru alone.
The tight timeline is also expected to create difficulties for voters in receiving the notices and preparing documents for the hearings. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) said they received the notices only on September 1, while distribution began on Wednesday. Given the volume of notices, they said distribution, in many cases, could continue until September 4 — just a day before the hearings begin. “Some people may get enough time, like at least two days, but some may not even get a day. While September 5 was decided as it is a Saturday to cause less inconvenience to the public, this cannot be done each time,” a BLO said.
Notices
There are also questions over the reasons cited in some of the notices. Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar, referring to the total number of notices, had said they would be served to voters with logical discrepancies or those whose details, or those of their family members, could not be mapped to the 2002 rolls. However, in several cases, voters who said they had provided the required details in their enumeration forms have also received notices, with the reasons cited not matching the details they had submitted.
For instance, in a notice accessed by The Hindu, a 71-year-old man from the Raichur constituency was issued a notice citing two reasons — that “the age gap between you and another progeny linked with the same parent is less than nine months” and that “the age difference between you and your parent, whose details are used to link you with the rolls prepared during the last SIR, is less than 15 years, that seems to be due to incorrect matching”.
However, the elector’s first son is 40 years old — born on June 1, 1984, while another son was born on August 26, 1985 — a gap of more than 13 months. Moreover, if the elector’s son is the person whose age creates that discrepancy, then the son should logically be the elector flagged for that particular discrepancy, not the father.
In another case in C.V. Raman Nagar, a voter and her mother were informed about the notices over the call, stating that they had not provided details for mapping. However, when checked, both their enumeration forms contained mapping details. In this case, voters were told that notice will be served, but it was yet not delivered, with electors not even knowing the hearing date.
The confusion seen during the enumeration phase, when several voters received calls asking them to collect enumeration forms and were unsure whether documents had to be submitted, also appears to have persisted into the notice process. Several voters said that BLOs had collected documents from them, saying this would “fasten the process” or “reduce discrepancies”. Some said they had received calls on Wednesday asking them to come to the polling station to collect their notices if they wanted them “on time”.
In many other cases, voters said BLOs had already collected documents, including caste certificates, Aadhaar cards, Class 10 certificates and transfer certificates. The voters, however, said they were unclear about why the documents were being collected or whether they were even required to submit them at this stage.
As per the guidelines, BLOs cannot collect any documents. Documents can be sought during the hearing process.

stories.headline: Canada fund buys 24% in tower firm for $1.3bn
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Canada’s La Caisse (formerly CDPQ) has bought a 24% stake in Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust for about Rs 12,100 crore ($1.3 billion). Brookfield and its entities will remain the largest shareholder in the company with a 37% stake.
Affiliates of GIC and British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI) are the other shareholders of Altius which owns and operates more than 2,58,000 telecom towers and sites across India.
“As India’s economy grows and more people and businesses rely on higher use of mobile data, the infrastructure behind those connections needs to keep pace,” said Emmanuel Jaclot, executive vice-president and head of infrastructure and sustainability at La Caisse. Altius provides the infrastructure that enables mobile operators to deliver 4G and 5G services. India is the world’s second-largest telecommunications market, and continued growth in mobile data use and 5G is increasing the need for digital infrastructure.
The deal comes ahead of Altius’ planned IPO which could raise about Rs 6,000 crore and transition from a privately listed infrastructure investment trust (InvIT) to a publicly listed InvIT. 
Last month, the company filed draft IPO papers with markets regulator Sebi.
Initially operating as Data Infrastructure Trust (DIT), it was rebranded as Altius in 2024 following the acquisition of American Tower’s (ATC) operations in India by a Brookfield-led consortium.
“Altius has built a scaled, nationwide platform that is in a leading position to meet India’s demand for mobile connectivity and 5G infrastructure. La Caisse’s investment brings another long-term institutional partner to the platform and reflects confidence in the strength of the business,” said Sam Pollock, CEO at Brookfield’s Infrastructure group. “Alongside our partners, we will continue to support Altius’ next phase of growth.”
Telecom tower companies are poised for growth in tenancy this fiscal and the next, driven by continued capital expenditure by telcos, analysts at Crisil said in a June report.
Additionally, revival in capex by select telcos, particularly in overlapping circles, will translate to incremental tenancies at existing tower sites, leading to improvement in the tenancy ratio in this fiscal and the next, after years of moderation.

stories.headline: High-value tech imports a worry: Auto cos
stories.bodyText:
New Delhi: India’s auto industry is warning that its next big vulnerability may not be vehicle production, but dependence on imported high-value technologies, with the chiefs of Hyundai Motor India and Maruti Suzuki calling for deeper localisation across semiconductors, battery cells, power electronics and other critical components.
At ACMA’s annual session, Hyundai Motor India MD & CEO Tarun Garg said India exported about $24 billion worth of auto components in 2025-26, but imported around $25.4 billion, resulting in a $1.4-billion trade deficit. “The concern goes beyond the deficit. Our exports remain concentrated in relatively mature technologies, while our imports are led by advanced, higher-value technologies, which may well define the future,” he said.
Garg said the industry needs to build domestic capability in semiconductor chips, rare-earth magnets, power electronics and battery cells, while stepping up investments in R&D and intellectual property. “Technology ownership is essential for strategic independence,” he said, adding that India must progress from exporting conventional components to advanced technologies and engineering capability.
Maruti Suzuki India MD & CEO Hisashi Takeuchi also identified “deep localisation” as critical to insulating the industry from global disruptions. 
“Deep localisation is about reducing our exposure to external disruptions by strengthening domestic capabilities and progressively owning a larger share of the value chain,” he said.
Takeuchi said changing global supply chains, govt support and India’s expanding automotive scale were creating a stronger case for localisation. Rising domestic demand and export opportunities, he said, now justify investments “including advanced technologies that were previously considered difficult to manufacture competitively in India.”
Both executives also stressed that localisation would have to extend beyond large OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. Takeuchi said stronger technology, engineering and quality capabilities among Tier-2 and Tier-3 suppliers would be critical, while Garg called for digitalisation, AI and shared learning to spread across the wider supplier ecosystem.

stories.headline: Reducing India’s exposure to U.S. tariff risks
stories.deck: The Lindsey O. Graham Act puts India under pressure, but export diversification and domestic reforms can cushion shocks
stories.bodyText:
The U.S. Senate recently passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, imposing sanctions and authorising additional tariffs and other restrictions related to Russia. Most concerning is a provision authorising tariffs of up to 100% on countries among the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or natural gas if they knowingly make new purchases after enactment. Though it still awaits House approval, enactment could have serious implications for India’s economic interests.
The Russian oil dilemma
India has diversified its energy supplies in recent years to reduce its crude import bill and gain strategic advantage amid global uncertainty, driving a sharp rise in Russian crude imports. Before the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Russian crude accounted for just 2% of India’s imports; it is now roughly half.
In 2026 alone, imports nearly doubled from 4.54 MMT in January to 8.96 MMT in May. While the strategy has helped secure supplies, it carries diplomatic costs, particularly in managing ties with the United States, which seeks to strongly discourage these imports. The U.S. Russia Sanctions Act reflects this pressure.
On July 24, before the bill’s introduction, the U.S. imposed forced-labour tariffs on 60 countries, including India, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, imposing an additional 10% tariff, a replacement of the expired 10% duty under Section 122, on India. If the Russia Sanctions Act becomes law, India’s cumulative tariff could reach 110%, making it one of the most heavily tariffed countries. Such high tariffs could affect India’s price competitiveness in the U.S., a major export market, leading to economic losses. China’s cumulative tariff could reach 112.5%, as both countries are major importers of Russian crude.
Trade simulations and results
To analyse the trade dynamics and possible way forward for India, two global trade simulations were conducted using the GTAP dataset and model, a global general equilibrium model that captures global linkages and country-level shocks. The first (sanction scenario) models a 110% U.S. tariff on India, with other countries facing forced-labour tariffs and China facing 112.5%. The second (diversification scenario) applies the same tariffs while India pursues export diversification, proxied by a full India-European Union free trade agreement (FTA).
The simulation results suggest that the proposed U.S. sanctions could have adverse consequences for the Indian economy. Under the sanction scenario, India’s welfare declines by nearly $47 billion, while GDP, output, domestic demand, exports, and imports all contract. Aggregate exports fall by 5.1% and imports by 5.2%, reflecting disrupted trade flows and weaker economic activity. The results indicate that a prolonged tariff-based confrontation with the U.S. could impose substantial costs on India’s growth and trade performance.
The picture changes considerably when India responds through export diversification. With a functional India-EU FTA, the economy turns around despite the same tariff environment. Welfare improves by $26.3 billion, GDP turns positive, and sectoral output and domestic demand recover by around 1%. Aggregate exports increase by 3.1%, while imports rise by a moderate 2.6%, indicating stronger production and trade integration with alternative markets.
The findings suggest that even if India continues procuring crude from Russia to strengthen its energy security, the adverse economic effects of U.S. tariffs can be mitigated to a large extent through export diversification. The India-EU FTA, used here as a proxy for diversification, demonstrates that India must increasingly look beyond the U.S. and expand its presence in alternative markets, even as the U.S. remains one of its largest export destinations.
The strategy to pursue
However, diversification is not a panacea. It depends on the ability of other markets to absorb additional Indian exports. Without adequate external demand, diversification may remain limited.
Therefore, export diversification must be complemented by sustained domestic reforms, including trade facilitation, removal of non-tariff barriers, improved logistics and standards, and movement up the goods quality ladder. Such a strategy would not only enhance India’s resilience to future geopolitical shocks but also strengthen its long-term export competitiveness.
Himanshu Jaiswal is a Consultant at the Centre for Social and Economic Progress, New Delhi. The views expressed are personal

stories.headline: Many layers: On onion produce, issues
stories.deck: Farmers need more storage facilities and better distribution networks
stories.bodyText:
Since the 1960s, India has developed a balancing-act habit: between keeping food prices affordably low for consumers and assuring farmers of remunerative prices, with the state’s interventions focused on managing this volatility in the short term. This is also why the government banned onion exports from December 2023 to May 2024, then imposed a $550/tonne minimum export price and a 40% export duty, reduced the duty to 20% in September 2024, and finally abolished it in April 2025. But erratic weather together with the lack of long-term relief has rendered the act increasingly awkward. From farmers’ point of view, the government often changes its mind after they have made important production-related decisions based on the expected price. On the other hand, during the bounteous rabi harvest, onion farmers in Maharashtra, the country’s principal supplier, had argued that the Centre’s procurement price of ₹12.35/kg would not cover the costs of cultivation. The Centre subsequently raised the price to up to ₹26.45/kg, but many farmers — including some who had had to sell at ₹1/kg earlier because of low quality and lack of storage, among other factors — were unable to capture the higher value, exposing the limits of intervening after prices have already collapsed and not reaching all farmers or grades of produce.
While the government has alluded to some price manipulation, the dominant issue remains that it keeps reacting instead of taking proactive measures, including improving storage options, maintaining a less erratic trade policy, moving stock more efficiently between regions, and protecting farmers against price shocks. The abnormal rainfall at the time of harvest and a 5%-7% drop in the kharif crop in Maharashtra, together with the well-known challenges associated with storing onions and maintaining large buffers, are simply among the pressures that highlighted the flaw this year. Further, Tamil Nadu’s targeted subsidy, to buy 1,000 tonnes of onions to distribute 1 kg per ration card at ₹35, will impose pressures on the Centre to maintain a steady supply. The move is commendably designed to discourage hoarding while allowing private retail prices to cool down. However, the State must also guard against the pitfalls of distributing onions through a dry-grain PDS network — its economic case could collapse if post-harvest losses, to which onion is more susceptible than, say, wheat or rice, exceed 10%-15% — and if the need arises to persist with the subsidy. Finally, if other States also adopt similar measures, the Central buffer could be quickly exhausted, more so given this year’s high storage losses of around 30%.

briefs.headline: Fresh investments by pvt cos jump 97% in Q1: CMIE
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Defying expectations, India’s private sector announced fresh investment projects worth Rs 15.4 lakh core in April-June quarter (Q1), a 97% jump compared to corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, latest CMIE data showed. This improvement in confidence was led by fresh investments in the electricity and services sectors, particularly in the IT segment.
Overall, the fresh capex (govt and private) in the economy touched a five-quarter high of Rs 17.8 lakh crore, even as fresh govt capex during Q1 FY27 declined 36% to Rs 2.4 lakh crore from Rs 3.9 lakh crore in Q1 FY26.
CMIE data showed new investments in the electricity and services sector in Q1 FY27 more than doubled to Rs 7.6 lakh crore from Rs 3.6 lakh crore and Rs 7.8 lakh crore from Rs 3.8 lakh crore respectively. In the services sector, new investments in IT sector alone rose nearly four times to Rs 6.5 lakh crore from Rs 1.6 lakh crore.
Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said share of capital formation in Q1 rose to 34.3% in nominal terms from 31.4% last year, with private capex “being driven by data centres and power.”
IDFC First Bank chief economist Gaura Sengupta said nascent signs of a pick-up in private capex are visible, with a “rise in bank lending to the infrastructure sector, capital goods imports and capital goods production.”
Fresh investments in the manufacturing sector, however, fell 40% to Rs 2.2 lakh crore from Rs 3.8 lakh crore, led by decline in investments in the food products industry, textiles, chemicals and construction materials. Construction sector also saw decline in investments to Rs 15,000 crore from Rs 40,900 crore. Data also showed that project completions remained nearly similar (Rs 2.4 lakh crore) in Q1 as compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year, while projects worth Rs 1 lakh crore were abandoned or shelved during Q1 FY27.

briefs.headline: Mahajan Imaging & Labs has entered a joint venture partnership with Neuberg Diagnostics
briefs.deck: The joint venture is structured to create a single, integrated diagnostic pathway for patients and clinicians.
briefs.bodyText:
Integrated diagnostic healthcare provider Mahajan Imaging & Labs has entered into a joint venture partnership with Neuberg Diagnostics to expand pathology and wellness services across north India.
“The collaboration has brought together Mahajan Imaging & Labs’ experience in radiology, nuclear medicine, PET CT and advanced diagnostics, established presence across Delhi-NCR and Jaipur, with Neuberg’s pathology and genomics capabilities, clinical and operational expertise and multi-market experience across India, the UAE, South Africa and the USA,’’ noted a release issued following the announcement.
Speaking to The Hindu, Harsh Mahajan, founder and chairman of Mahajan Imaging & Labs, said, “The partnership will look to make diagnostics more accessible and affordable and work towards greater integration across pathology, imaging, nuclear medicine and genomics. We wanted to scale up pathology without losing quality. Neuberg’s expertise in pathology is what we looked at while deciding this partnership. This association allows us to accelerate that existing capability by bringing in additional scale, infrastructure and expertise.’’
The joint venture is structured to create a single, integrated diagnostic pathway for patients and clinicians. Instead of sending samples to different vendors for imaging versus advanced pathology, the combined network aims to offer end-to-end testing—from routine blood work and advanced molecular tests to PET-CT and nuclear medicine—under coordinated protocols and shared digital systems. This should reduce turnaround times, cut down on repeat sampling, and make it easier for doctors to get a consolidated report that links imaging findings with pathology and genomic data.
For patients in Delhi-NCR and nearby cities, the immediate visible change will likely be branding and lab consolidation. The collaboration promises to offer faster reporting, better tracking of samples, and fewer errors due to manual handling.

briefs.headline: Sugar mills reassure adequate availability during festival season
briefs.deck: For most of the 2025–26 sugar season, mills have realised prices well below the normal cost of production of ₹42 per kg; the prices were ₹39.5–₹40.0 per kg in June and roughly ₹41- 41.5 per kg through August 2026
briefs.bodyText:
The Indian Sugar and Bio-energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) and the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories (NFCSF) have reassured that domestic sugar availability will meet the festival demand.
The ex-mill prices have cooled by nearly 30% from peak with government efforts.
For most of the 2025–26 sugar season, mills have realised prices well below the normal cost of production of ₹42 per kg. The prices were ₹39.5–₹40.0 per kg in June and roughly ₹41- 41.5 per kg through August 2026.
The brief surge to ₹49–₹50 per kg witnessed in the third week of August applied to fractional volume of just about three lakh tonnes.
Retail prices have cooled down to around ₹62 per kg, i.e., by almost 5% from its peak, and is expected to go further downwards.

briefs.headline: VinFast said to put brakes on making some cars in India, sources and memo say
briefs.deck: The suspension marks another setback for loss-making VinFast, which turned to India after difficulties in gaining market share in the U.S. and Europe
briefs.bodyText:
VinFast suspended plans to make three electric vehicles in India and ordered suppliers to halt work on the projects while it reviews costs, as per sources and a memo reviewed by Reuters — a year after Vietnam’s automaker entered the crucial growth market.
The manufacturer VinFast asked suppliers to “hold all activities” on three programmes, including a two-door SUV called VF 3 — expected to be its most competitive model in the market — and VF 6 and VF 7 SUVs, which it imports as kits from Vietnam and assembles in the country.
The suspension marks another setback for loss-making VinFast, which turned to India after difficulties in gaining market share in the U.S. and Europe.
The suspension of plans to locally make the three vehicles in India has not been previously reported. Vinfast opened its first factory outside Vietnam in southern India last year and pledged to invest $2 billion, as it sought to build a regional manufacturing base serving South Asia, West Asia and Africa.
After publication of this story, VinFast told Reuters the change in production strategy relates to future models, and it will continue to import and assemble the VF 6 and VF 7 now sold in India.
VinFast also said it plans to develop India-specific models rather than just bringing in existing global models a move that it says will allow it to accelerate local sourcing.
While VinFast has publicly stated increasing local sourcingfrom India, including through partnerships with domesticsuppliers, plans to manufacture the VF 3, VF 6 and VF 7 in thecountry have not previously been disclosed and were described toReuters by people familiar with the matter.
“India is an important market in VinFast’s long-termbusiness and manufacturing strategy,” a company representative told Reuters in a statement, adding that based on market research and consumer feedback it is making “appropriate adjustments” to its products to “better meet the needs of Indian customers”.
VinFast’s struggle to break into the world’s third-largest car market echoes challenges faced by others, including Volkswagen and Nissan, which did not achieve the kind of scale that has helped companies such as Suzuki and Hyundai succeed.
In a July memo to suppliers, the automaker said it decided to “temporarily” put on hold all development work related to the VF 3, VF 6 and VF 7. Locally developing and sourcing parts would have allowed VinFast to avoid expensive imports and price itscars more competitively.
SUPPLIER INVESTMENTS
The memo also asked suppliers to provide a detailed breakdown of the “total amount invested to date” on the projects that require payment or reimbursement from VinFast across cost categories such as tooling, engineering and materials, along with “supporting documentation where available”.
VinFast did not meet its planned costs for developing partsin India for the three cars, which is why it stopped the work, one of the sources said.
Both sources declined to be named as they are not authorised to speak to the media.
Backed by Vietnam’s largest conglomerate Vingroup, VinFast launched in India in September 2025 with its VF 6 and VF7 electric SUVs. Its India factory has an initial annual production capacity of 50,000 cars and is scalable to 150,000 units.
The automaker has so far sold about 10,000 cars in India, including to its affiliate ride-hailing company Green SM.

briefs.headline: La Caisse acquires 24% stake in Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust for ₹12,100 crore
briefs.deck: Global investment group La Caisse and Brookfield... announced that La Caisse has invested approximately ₹121 billion to acquire a 24% stake in Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust, said a statement
briefs.bodyText:
Canadian Pension Fund La Caisse has purchased a 24% stake in India’s biggest independent telecom infrastructure firm Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust for about ₹12,100 crore, the firm said on Wednesday (September 2, 2026).
Altius owns and operates more than 2,58,000 telecom towers and sites across India, giving it a nationwide presence.
“Global investment group La Caisse, and Brookfield... announced that La Caisse has invested approximately ₹121 billion [CAD 1.76 billion] to acquire a 24% stake in Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust,” the statement said.
With the transaction now complete, Brookfield remains Altius’ largest investor, alongside La Caisse and existing shareholders who are affiliates of GIC and British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI), the statement said.
“This is a sector we know well through our investments in telecom towers and digital infrastructure around the world. With Altius, we are investing in an attractive market through an established platform, alongside Brookfield and other institutional partners with whom we have longstanding relationships,” Emmanuel Jaclot, Executive Vi-P and Head of Infrastructure and Sustainability at La Caisse, said.
Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust, formerly Data Infrastructure Trust, is a Sebi-registered infrastructure investment trust (InvIT). Altius is engaged in the provision of passive telecom infrastructure services in India.
“La Caisse’s investment brings another long-term institutional partner to the platform and reflects confidence in the strength of the business. Alongside our partners, we will continue to support Altius’ next phase of growth by deploying our owner-operator capabilities and disciplined, long-term approach to infrastructure investing,” Sam Pollock, CEO of Brookfield’s Infrastructure group, said.

briefs.headline: Rs 30 lakh salary, missed ITR after job switch; why ITAT cancelled Rs 3.74 lakh tax penalty
briefs.deck: What appeared to be a filing lapse eventually turned into a tax penalty of Rs 3.74 lakh. The Income Tax Department took a strict view of the matter, maintaining that had the non-filing not been detected, Aggarwal might not have filed his ITR at all. This, in turn, would have meant that his salary and interest income remained unreported.
briefs.bodyText:
Switching jobs comes with the need for increased vigilance on the income tax front. But what if your Form 16 is delayed and you are unable to file your tax return in time and the 
Income Tax Department
 imposes a penalty?
That’s what happened with Pravesh Aggarwal, a resident of Indrapuram in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. Aggarwal changed jobs and earned a salary of Rs 30 lakh; however he failed to file his income tax return by the deadline. The reason was that he had not received his Form 16 from his previous employer in time.
What appeared to be a filing lapse eventually turned into a tax penalty of Rs 3.74 lakh. The Income Tax Department took a strict view of the matter, maintaining that had the non-filing not been detected, Aggarwal might not have filed his ITR at all. This, in turn, would have meant that his salary and interest income remained unreported.
Aggarwal eventually challenged the matter and, after a prolonged legal battle, succeeded in winning the case before the Delhi bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).
Why did the Income Tax Department send the penalty tax notice?
Aggarwal had switched jobs during the financial year 2018-19, in the middle of the year. From his new employment, he earned a salary of Rs 30.22 lakh, according to an ET report. 
However, during the transition between his old and new jobs, he could not obtain the necessary documents, including Form 16, from his employer before the deadline for filing his ITR.
Although the Form 16 was not available to him, Aggarwal’s Form 26AS contained the details of the TDS that had been deducted by his employers. Based on this, he believed that since the relevant income and TDS were already reflected in Form 26AS, there would be no issue if he did not separately file an ITR. He therefore did not submit his return within the prescribed time.
The matter resurfaced later when the Income Tax Department reopened Aggarwal’s tax assessment under Section 147 after passing an order under Section 148A(d) on April 19, 2023.
Following the tax notice, Aggarwal filed his ITR on May 8, 2023. In the return submitted in response to the notice, he declared a total income of Rs 30.22 lakh.
The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) examined this return and subsequently initiated penalty proceedings against Aggarwal for under-reporting of income, on the ground that he had not filed an ITR earlier.
During the penalty proceedings, Aggarwal explained that he had acted under a bona fide belief that his tax liability had already been discharged because both his employers had deducted TDS from his salary. On that basis, he believed there was no further requirement for him to file an ITR.
The Income Tax Assessing Officer, however, did not accept Aggarwal’s explanation. The AO imposed a penalty of Rs 3.74 lakh, which was 50% of the tax on the concealed income, on the grounds that Aggarwal had under-reported his income and had failed to file his original ITR within the deadline.
Aggarwal challenged the penalty before the Commissioner of Appeals (CIT A), but his arguments were rejected there as well. The Rs 3.74 lakh penalty was consequently confirmed, prompting Aggarwal to take the matter to ITAT Delhi.
Why ITAT Delhi ruled in the taxpayer’s favour
Anubhav Sharma, Judicial Member, and Manish Agarwal, Accountant Member, of ITAT Delhi observed that a genuine salaried employee should not face a disproportionate penalty for failing to file an ITR, particularly when the employer has already deducted TDS from the salary and there has been no under-reporting of income.
Representing the Income Tax Department, Jitendra Singh backed the decisions taken by the lower authorities. He argued that if a notice under Section 148 had not been served on Aggarwal, the income in question would have escaped taxation. According to Singh, Aggarwal would then not have filed his ITR and the salary and interest income would not have been reported.
Aggarwal ultimately secured relief from ITAT Delhi on May 13, 2026.
Anubhav Sharma explained that sub-section 2 of Section 270A provides that ‘under-reporting income’ arises when a taxpayer declares an amount that is lower than the actual income earned.
In Aggarwal’s case, however, the income that he eventually reported and declared was accepted by the Income Tax Department. The ITAT Delhi therefore observed that the matter could not be treated as one where a taxpayer had disclosed an amount lower than his actual income.
The Tribunal also noted that Aggarwal was acting under a bona fide belief that the tax payable on his salary had already been deducted at source by his respective employers. The TDS details were also appearing in Form 26AS, leading him to believe that he had complied with his tax obligation by disclosing the income earned during the year.
According to ITAT Delhi, Aggarwal had a bona fide and genuine belief that there had been neither any misrepresentation nor suppression of facts. The income was duly reflected in Form No. 26AS on the Income Tax Department’s portal, and the Department was already aware of those details. In these circumstances, the Tribunal held that there was no question of under-reporting of income.
The Tribunal further explained that Section 270A(2) can result in under-reporting of income only where the income reassessed is higher than the income that had previously been determined and assessed.
In this case, at least prima facie, the income assessed under Section 148 was not higher than the income declared by Aggarwal. ITAT Delhi therefore held that the case could not be considered one involving misrepresentation either.
Based on these findings, ITAT Delhi directed that the Rs 3.74 lakh penalty imposed under Section 270A be deleted. It also allowed all the grounds of appeal raised by Aggarwal.

briefs.headline: RBI may prioritise closing dollar shorts with FCNR(B) inflow
briefs.bodyText:
The central bank may prioritise closing its $137 billion open short forward dollar positions , with the FCNR(B) deposits received , according to experts and industry insiders.
“The RBI has an outstanding short forward position of USD 137 Bn. If the RBI decides to not roll over the outstanding positions the INR liquidity will be absorbed from the banking system and RBI may use the excess FX reserves generated from the FCNR (B) scheme for delivering the dollars,” said Shashi Dhar, Chief General Manager of Treasury & Global Markets at Bank of Baroda. Short forward dollars are currency derivative contracts where RBI commits to sell dollars at a future date at a predetermined rate. This is used to defend the rupee without drawing down spot reserves immediately.
The central bank had already begun absorbing rupee liquidity to make sure call rates don’t fall below policy rate, he continued. Mr. Dhar further said that liquidity is at ₹6.5 lakh crore and RBI may absorb some of this to make sure short-term money supply does not feed into inflation and keep borrowing cost aligned with policy rate. This became important as the RBI signalled an expectation of higher inflation, in its monetary policy committee meeting minutes.
Meanwhile, banks may be inclined to use this to “bolster their asset-side books and reduce their dependence on wholesale deposits in the immediate term” Mr.Dhar said, adding that in the long term, they can use the excessive liquidity to fund credit growth.
One of the predominant reasons for introducing the FCNR(B) scheme was to arrest increasing foreign exchange rate. The rupee has become cheaper by 7.22% against the dollar, trading at around ₹96 against the greenback.
Economists however express their concerns regarding structural depreciation of the rupee even amid whopping FCNR(B) inflows. “FCNR is one of the aspects that we tried to consider to create a solution to a problem that was a perfect storm but for us to become extremely secure with the way we manage our currency, we will need to get embedded in global value chains,” said Garima Kapoor , Deputy Head of Research and Economist at Elara Capital. “ In my view, FCNR or no FCNR, I do not think the rupee has a pathway for structural appreciation,” she said.
